name: Scrape eBay listings for demand and price bands with Bright Data, GPT-5.6, Google Sheets and Slack

parameters.content:
## Find the eBay listings that are actually selling, and what they sell for

Give it a few search terms and it comes back with the listings that are moving, each with the numbers that say so and the price band they sit in.

### How it works
A weekly schedule sends one eBay search per term through Bright Data's discovery API. It takes a minute or two, so the workflow uses the asynchronous API properly: it triggers the search, then polls the snapshot on a Wait loop with a five-minute cap until the rows are ready.

Listings are grouped by search term and condition, because a refurbished unit and a new one are not the same market, and a band with fewer than four listings is skipped rather than compared against a median of one. Each listing is then scored on units sold against its band median, people watching it today, carts it is sitting in, stock left, and where its price sits in the band. Those watcher and cart counts are on the public page and are not in eBay's own APIs, which is the reason this reads the listing. GPT-5.6 turns the keyword-soup title into a brand, model and product type, and writes the closing brief.

Listings reported recently are skipped for thirty days, the whole list lands in Google Sheets, and a ranked digest goes to Slack.

### Setup
Add a Bright Data API key as a Header Auth credential (`Authorization` / `Bearer YOUR_KEY`), connect OpenAI, Google Sheets and Slack, then set your search terms and channel in Set Search Config.

### Customization
Raise min_demand_score for a shorter, stronger list, or point search_keywords at a niche you already source in.

## 1. Pick the search terms
A few eBay searches on a weekly schedule. Everything you would tune lives in one config node.

## 2. Search eBay asynchronously
Bright Data runs one eBay search per term. Eight listings took 96 seconds in testing, so this polls the snapshot until the rows are ready.

## 3. Score demand inside a price band
Listings are grouped by term and condition, then scored on units sold, watchers, carts and stock against that band's median.

## 4. Drop the ones you have had
The sheet doubles as the do-not-repeat list, so a listing reported recently stays out of this week's digest.

## 5. Read the keyword-soup titles
The model turns an eBay title into a brand, model and product type. Every number stated as fact comes from a field.

## 6. Deliver
One sheet row per listing, which is what the next run reads back, plus a ranked Slack digest.

## Start with two search terms
Every term is a separate eBay search and adds to the wait. Units sold is a lifetime total for that listing, not a weekly rate.

parameters.text:
=Read this eBay listing title and say what the product actually is.

eBay titles are written to be searched, not read, so they stack brand, model,
features and filler into one line. Pull the product out of it.

Use only what is in the title and the specifications. If the title does not say
the brand, leave `brand` empty rather than guessing from the model name.
`is_bundle` is true only when the listing is plainly several items sold together.

Title: {{ $json.title }}
Brand field on the listing: {{ $json.brand || 'not set' }}
Condition: {{ $json.condition }}
Specifications: {{ $json.spec_summary || 'none listed' }}

`product_type` should be two or three plain lower case words: "mechanical
keyboard", "wireless mouse", "keycap set".
`key_features` should be two to four short lower case phrases a buyer would
actually compare on: "hot swappable", "75% layout", "bluetooth".
